summary: RunCLICommand (internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go), the command-mirror shellout used by every non-typed MCP tool, now includes both stderr and stdout in the returned error when a failed subprocess wrote to both -- previously it picked stderr alone whenever non-empty, silently discarding a non-trivial stdout. A regen must keep the three-way switch (stderr-only, stdout-only, both) rather than reverting to stderr-priority.
reason: Marking workouts a critical sync resource (see workouts-marked-critical-resource.json) made this pre-existing gap concretely reachable for the first time: a failed `workflow archive --json` now exits non-zero with a short cobra "Error: ..." summary on stderr, while the actual sync_error event naming which resource failed and why only exists in stdout's NDJSON stream. Live-tested: a caller got "1 critical resource(s) failed to sync: workouts" with no way to learn the underlying reason, where the same failure previously (when it exited 0) showed the full diagnosis in the visible event stream.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. New test TestRunCLICommandIncludesBothStreamsOnFailure drives a helper script that writes distinct content to both streams and asserts both appear in the returned error; existing stderr-only/stdout-only/bounded-output tests still pass unmodified.
